name: Bright Light Blue
lede: Bright Light Blue is a vivid cyan, a screen color far more saturated than almost anything on a canvas.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name is a plain description from the xkcd color survey, where thousands of people named colors on screen, and the swatch sits nearest to [[aqua]] [1]. It is a screen-born name with no pigment or dye behind it [1].

The books we hold mention a bright light blue only in an optics passage that Gage quotes from Goethe's Theory of Colours: a dark window bar seen against a dull grey sky grows colored edges, a light-blue one on its upper side [3]. That is an effect of the eye, not a pigment [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole, but it fits a color this saturated: nothing in oil or watercolor reaches it easily [2].
